inputs.original_text:
Look, we need to be completely clear about what’s actually going on here when those at the top try to hide behind institutional rhetoric. President John Mahama wants us to buy into the narrative that the rules of this system are just naturally tied to our cultural ethos and collective agreement, but we know exactly who writes these laws and whose interests they actually protect. 

When systemic inequality is baked right into the very institutions of our society, simply talking about upholding the rule of law just means locking in the status quo that keeps marginalized and vulnerable communities down. He stands there and declares that he took an oath to uphold [...], but an oath to a structurally unjust system isn't enough when human rights are on the line globally. If we don't radically reform these institutions to center labor, justice, and true equity, this talk about legal frameworks is just smoke and mirrors designed to protect the powerful from accountability.
inputs.modified_text: We need to open our eyes and stop buying into the narrative pushed by President John Mahama that the rules of this system are just naturally tied to our cultural ethos and collective agreement. We know exactly who writes these laws and whose interests they actually protect. When systemic inequality is baked right into the very institutions of our society, simply talking about upholding the rule of law just means locking in the status quo that keeps marginalized and vulnerable communities down. He stands there and declares that he took an oath to uphold [...], but an oath to a structurally unjust system isn't enough when human rights are on the line globally. If we don't radically reform these institutions to center labor, justice, and true equity, this talk about legal frameworks is just smoke and mirrors designed to protect the powerful from accountability.
